definition: A method for injecting information about token order into transformer models, which otherwise have no inherent sense of sequence position.
details: Because self-attention processes all tokens simultaneously and has no built-in notion of order, positional encodings (sinusoidal, learned, or rotary) are added to token embeddings to preserve sequence information.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — Positional Encoding — is what makes everything else possible.
